current.text: Cleveland lost Dennis Schroder, Keon Ellis, Max Strus and Dean Wade this offseason. All were rotation players.
He is projected as the sixth man behind a starting five of James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
Experts expect his minutes to stay high and his role to grow in year three. He could play close to starter's minutes and cover positions one through three.
Last season he shot about 45% from three, up from 35% the season before. Over his final 16 games he shot 37%.
Experts do not expect the 45% three-point shooting to repeat. One thinks above 40% is still possible.
In a bench role he projects around 150 to 170 overall. A 20-game absence by a player ahead of him would push him well past that.
He is a late-round swing pick and a possible flyer if his role grows. He matters more in 14-team and deeper leagues.

The experts disagree on his upside. Josh is not convinced the bigger role turns into fantasy value and wants a bigger sample. Danny sees a next step of 15 to 16 points on good efficiency as a secondary creator.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With our March 28 end date, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in the fantasy playoff weeks. The two-game week is the finals week.

durable.text: His production was strong when teammates were out and faded when they returned.
Last season he had a high passing turnover rate and low assist numbers.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD and rank him outside our 144 drafted players (Yahoo 233, ESPN 191). In our 12-team league he is at most a 1 USD last-round flyer, and more likely a waiver add. His projected line is close to neutral in every category, but it brings little in AST, STL or BLK. The 37% three-point shooting over his final 16 games and the expert range of 150 to 170 in a bench role both point to a waiver-level player unless injuries to Harden, Mitchell or Watson open up starter's minutes. Early in the season, check how many minutes he gets as sixth man and whether his three-point percentage stays near 40%. Also keep in mind the two-game finals week and Cleveland's league-high number of back-to-backs.
